intent.final: Felix is the pilot of implementation, and it is for anyone's project on any device. The founder owns what gets built: thesis, priorities, and approval at genuinely high-risk or irreversible boundaries. Felix owns how it gets built: tools, installs, execution shape, tracking and correction. It intervenes rather than advises, escalates almost nothing, and stays quiet in the middle of a session. It governs engineering only. On 08-10 the founder framed it as Phase 1 of his guidebook and a future sub-OS under a chief agent. On 2026-09-22/23 he replaced that with 'a product for other people's projects', judged by whether it survives a stranger adopting it, built first on Claude Code and host-independent by design, with engineering-only kept (#290). Commercialisation follows quality rather than leading it (46af4fa6 03:13Z; roadmap §1).

interaction_lessons.lesson: When the person who owns the what says 'don't exempt yourself from your own rules', apply the mechanical checks to yourself. Do not turn it into making them the approver of every change, and do not write that approval into the option they pick. Ask what the rule is for before choosing how to honour it.

2026-08-14T01:28Z (fe3fffd4): Felix cannot earn autonomy from the red engine work it most needs to do (a bootstrap deadlock). Replace the green streak with an earned-autonomy record, but keep changes that widen Felix's own authority behind a separate, explicit, auditable gate.

Identify the trusted engine by git commit. Put merge enforcement on the trusted side. `felix install` becomes promotion of accepted main only. The `installed` check moves after the merge. intent.final: Felix never certifies itself. The engine the project has accepted (V_n) judges each candidate (V_n+1) from outside the candidate's tree. A change to the authority root goes to the founder permanently, through an enforcement point that cannot be skipped. Work can be finished from any checkout. Felix designs, stress-tests and maintains the trust chain itself, and brings the founder in only for architecture-level choices.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Before building on a recorded decision, re-read the record that owns it and test the build against the failure modes it states. A decision the owner already paid for is the cheapest review there is.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The agent built route 2 on 2026-08-16 without reading §4a, which on 08-14 said install-before-green makes the candidate the judge. It cost a deployed rollback and a 44-agent review (b2baf090 21:59Z; 0c.md).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Never hand the person who owns the what a 'how' as the next step. When a question sits inside the system (how a judge is pinned, what evidence stands in for a check), derive the answer first with a blind independent pass, then bring only the architecture-level consequence.
interaction_lessons.evidence: fe3fffd4 01:43Z ('your call on how base-version evaluation gets achieved') was followed by the founder's 12k-character design at 02:02Z. The component questions at b2baf090 03:53Z/03:57Z were followed by 'stress test it yourself first' at 03:58Z. The blind deriver then beat the agent's own design in about 10 minutes (04:10Z).

interaction_lessons.lesson: When an outside constraint (a plan, a price, a platform limit) seems to block a design, research the alternatives before parking the work on the owner as a purchase decision. Separate the property the purchase buys from the property the design needs.
interaction_lessons.evidence: Pro was parked on the founder at fe3fffd4 05:42Z and b2baf090 09:46Z. His question whether GitHub Pro was the only viable solution (09:52Z) got four routes and 'Pro buys unavoidable, not trustworthy' in about a minute (09:59Z).

interaction_lessons.lesson: A decided and specced direction stays at the top of the carried queue until it is built, or until it is explicitly deferred with a reason, an owner and a date. Re-ordering it behind new work, or letting a new priority displace it, without saying so leads later sessions to route around it and eventually write the opposite.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The spec was written 2026-08-18 (#52). The same day §0d put the auto-merge guard 'before §0b'. The founder's 08-19 routing redirect then took the queue, and #2 was absent from every handoff 'next' list from 0aa to 0ba. 0al.md and the agent's 09-04 answer called the failure not a defect, and merges went through gh pr merge. The build came on 09-13 (614500d8 22:57Z: 'decided on 2026-08-18 and never built').

interaction_lessons.lesson: Don't call a trust mechanism done until its default path has run the way the owner will run it. Overrides and fixtures test a different program from the one that ships.
interaction_lessons.evidence: 'Route 2 is done and verified in all three places' (b2baf090 01:18Z), then the founder's own felix merge failed on an env-var default that no assertion ran (01:48Z).

interaction_lessons.lesson: A known hole in a trust mechanism is a defect with an owner and a date, not a disclaimer in a comment. Name it as something to close, or it survives until an adversary finds it.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The FELIX_KERNEL override was described as a limit on 2026-08-16 (b2baf090 20:55Z) and in 0c.md. A refuter filed it as #260 only on 09-17, and it was fixed in #263.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When an open decision keeps being re-listed as 'yours' and never answered, change how it is posed: state the default Felix will take, the consequence, and when it will act. Otherwise it goes invisible, and the gap it guards stays open.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The wall for felix-home was posed again at fa389b5e 19:05Z, fe3fffd4 02:09Z and 05:42Z, b2baf090 09:46Z, the 0bc/0bf next-lists and 85410a9f 11:17Z. The founder never answered it after 'route 2.'. On 09-21 enforcement was found to be floor-only.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Before asking the owner for an act that a platform rule must accept (a required review, an approval), check that the rule will count his act. A solo operator cannot approve his own pull request.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The agent asked the founder to review Elenchus#20 (11053b61 04:00Z). His approval could not count because he authored it (05:53Z). It took two more founder turns, and in the end he dropped required approvals to 0 (18:25Z).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Read the losing findings of a review before summarizing it. A refutation stage tuned to kill noise also kills real constraints.
interaction_lessons.evidence: Round 2 was reported as '1 of 37 survived' (b2baf090 05:15Z). Only the founder's question (06:19Z) led the agent to find four build constraints in the refuted pile.

Separating 'unavoidable' from 'trustworthy' (b2baf090 09:59Z) was a real architectural insight that kept the founder from paying for the wrong half.

Mutation-testing the resolver: reverting to the vacuous design turned six assertions red (b2baf090 01:05Z). Assertions were rewritten to name which blocker fired.

The founder's hedge idea became a measured method, with the prediction stated before the result: 1 blind agent at 160k tokens against 41 adversarial agents at 4.3M, recorded as a hypothesis before it was confirmed (memory blind-derivation-beats-adversarial-review.md).

The escalation register was fixed as a standing contract in the same turn the founder stated it (memory escalate-at-architecture-level.md), with #2 reframed as 'Felix can only be worked on in one place'.

intent.initial: On 2026-08-10 the agent asked what to build next and how far Felix should go on judgment calls. The founder chose 'Execution shape first' and 'Let Felix call a model when it must judge', over 'Refuse and record only' and 'Refuse, record, and recommend' (fa389b5e AskUserQuestion result, 21:18:38Z). The agent's own description of the model option said it breaks the second invariant. At 21:19:23Z the founder wrote in capitals that Felix 'IS NOT A RECOMMENDER' and must interfere and handle build direction with bare-minimum input. The intent: Felix uses judgment and acts. It is not a rule lookup that only refuses.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When the person who owns the what picks an option from a menu you wrote, build that option. If you believe a narrower version is right, ask 'I will build a narrower version because X; confirm or override' before committing it to doctrine. Do not label the narrower version 'as chosen', and do not let the code fall back further to the option they declined.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Never present a rule you wrote as the owner's own or as a fact about the machine. Name who set it and whether it can be overridden, so the owner can tell a real platform limit from a self-imposed ceiling. Check especially before using it to strike part of the owner's own spec.

intent.final: Felix owns every 'how': mechanics, design choices, tidying, due upkeep and execution shape. It decides these, records the rejected alternative where it can be overturned, and reports what was done. It stops only where a revert cannot reach (secrets, CI holding keys, stores, money, autonomy grants, published artifacts) or where the change alters what Felix is. When it does stop, it arrives with the analysis done and a yes/no recommendation, framed as a change to Felix's architecture. Otherwise it writes the item down and keeps working. The number of asks must fall. Standing directions become mechanisms rather than repeated prose. Every founder turn that does the agent's job, and every declined suggestion, counts as a Felix failure. The founder-Felix interaction is the measuring instrument, so the rules learned from it belong in Felix for any user, not in one user's assistant memory.

outcome.evidence:
The words of the intent were delivered quickly and well: a verified revert rule, doctrine lines, five memory entries each written within minutes of the correction, and on 09-12 a real mechanism (overnight mode, #222). The behaviour and the measurement were not.

(1) The founder had to do the agent's job in 17 of 43 turns across six weeks. By period: 7 of 19 on 08-10..13, 6 of 9 on 08-18..19, 4 of 7 on 09-02..13, and 0 of 8 on 09-22..23. The last week's turns were mostly new ideas, and its closes still handed tidying back (an unpushed commit on the home's main, 11053b61 18:15Z). The don't-stop direction was restated in prose at the start of at least five sessions before it became a mechanism.

(2) The declared objective was never computable. `felix merge` writes 'escalated' with an empty session (engine/harness/felix:1441), and all 18 rows read 'unknown' through 2026-09-22. The audit found this on 09-02 (2be823c0 22:55Z) and nothing fixed it. Asks a session invents, the common source per 0f27ee6e 07:24Z, were never instrumented. No command prints the objective or its pair. By 09-21 a design doc named a different outcome measure (verified milestones per human prompt, missed escalations). On 09-23 the founder effectively replaced it with leakage per session, which lives only in the assistant's memory.

(3) The founder's own verdict on 09-23 is that interaction rules land in the wrong place: per-user memory, not Felix. The Elenchus handoff shows it concretely: on 08-19 it still listed PR #5 and tidying as the founder's, after felix-home's HANDOFF had ruled both out.

(4) The escalated PR #5 got a 'merge it' recommendation on 08-13 that the founder never answered. Product sessions kept re-listing it as his instead of re-posing the yes/no, and it went stale and conflicting.

interaction_lessons.lesson: A mechanical stop is not a question for the person who owns the what. When a guard refuses, run the check it cannot run and arrive with a yes/no recommendation. Never forward the refusal as 'your call'. If the yes/no goes unanswered, re-pose it; do not let it rot on a 'yours' list.
interaction_lessons.evidence: PR #5's execute escapes went to the founder twice as 'founder's call', and one command then showed zero secrets referenced (4c96b238 08:48Z, 08:51Z). The recommendation was never answered, and Elenchus handoffs re-listed it as his until it conflicted (08-19). #285 on 09-22 shows the doctrine working (11053b61 21:31Z).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Before asking, sort the question. Does it turn on the owner's preference or authority (what gets built, spend, grants, anything a revert cannot reach), or on a fact or design choice you can establish? Decide the second kind, and put the reasoning and the rejected alternative where they can be overturned.
interaction_lessons.evidence: #227's hash question 'really breaks the felix thesis' (c79569a0 2026-09-13T00:05Z). Asking which defect to attack first (0f27ee6e 07:24Z). The auto-merge threshold ask (0f27ee6e 07:20Z). 25 of 27 structured questions with a recommended option were answered with it.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Due upkeep and tidying never go on the owner's to-do list, including branch cleanup and unpushed commits. Do them and report them done. Re-read this rule before writing any 'yours next' close-out, including after a compaction.
interaction_lessons.evidence: Corrected 2026-08-11T00:49Z (fa389b5e), 2026-09-12T08:58Z and 09:55Z, and again 2026-09-13T18:43Z (c79569a0). The 09-13 close came about 25 hours after the correction, which the compaction summary carried. It recurred on 2026-09-22T18:15Z (11053b61).

interaction_lessons.lesson: When an escalation is warranted, frame it as what changes about the system: what it can now do, what it stops doing, what class of work stops needing a person. Write it so a person reads it as a want and a coordinating agent could act on it. Never frame it at component level (thresholds, which proof, which bytes).

interaction_lessons.lesson: A metric you declare must be computable on the day you declare it. Test the key that joins numerator to denominator, and instrument first the source you control, which is your own asks.

notes:
The turn labels were read from the transcripts. Turns were selected because they bear on where Felix stops, so 17/43 is a leakage rate for this strand, not a session rate. Merge-authority turns are left to E15. By period, leakage was 7 of 19 turns on 08-10..13, 6 of 9 on 08-18..19, 4 of 7 on 09-02..13 and 0 of 8 on 09-22..23. Written rules did not reduce recurrence until the last week. The last week's founder turns were new ideas, while the agent's 09-22 close still handed tidying back, which may flatter it.

The recommended-option statistic was recomputed by tool_use id over the nine sessions (91c15299, fa389b5e, 4c96b238, b2baf090, 0f27ee6e, 2be823c0, 59d07e04, c79569a0, 11053b61): 46 answered, 27 with a '(Recommended)' option, 25 of 27 picked, and 4 free-text overrides. The earlier askstat.py missed one answer format. The figure suggests most structured asks were decidable by the agent, though a person can accept a well-argued recommendation that still needed their authority.

The 09-05 stack.tsv question is labelled judgment because it decided which grounding authorises unattended medium-risk installs, an autonomy grant. It is still a channel defect, having come as prose. Bazaar reversed a founder answer on evidence: its checkout took commits through 09-18, so the 'done' premise was false. That fits 'Felix owns how', but the record's framing of a handback is not clearly sourced.

The objective's history is the sharpest single finding. It was declared on 08-13 after 18 seconds of founder input and found uncomputable on 09-02. A different outcome measure was proposed on 09-21 and leakage was adopted on 09-23, only in assistant memory, while engine comments (felix:1432, next.sh:9) still anchor ranking on it. The overnight session's felix_say passes the session id (hooks/stop), so the key was available to the escalation writer too. No files outside the scratchpad were written.

Architectural weight. This episode changed what Felix is, not only where it is hosted. It split doctrine from memory: invariant 6 became 'a home holds doctrine', and memory now roots at $HOME/.felix, never at the checkout. It fixed the publishing model as a history-free snapshot of engine/ plus projects/felix, never the working repository, and named 'is this state, or is this consent' as the test for what ships. It also gave up the free route to an unavoidable required-status check. Route 2 (#45) answered the other half (a trustworthy judge), so felix-home still has no server-side wall.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When the person who owns the what asks for something automatic, don't let a latency or cost question about implementation decide the architecture. And don't endorse a choice that drops what they asked for against your own measurement. Decide the mechanism, or escalate only the outcome trade, and say plainly what is lost.

Pattern across the episode. The agent repeatedly narrowed the design to what it could build or prove cheaply, and the founder widened it back (the agent's own words at 06:30Z). Twenty days later both are unpushed, while the engine grew a 9-state obligation machine around them. - The hooks have no off switch.
- The gate is Elenchus's only CI and was green on 30 of 30 runs.

Once it had the founder's intent, it tested designs with counterfactual walks against the live repositories. The walks caught two of its own false claims and found the real entrypoint gap.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When the person who owns the what overrides a recommendation, record the override and their stated purpose that same turn, in the same place the recommendation lives. Otherwise later sessions keep acting on advice that was already overruled.
interaction_lessons.evidence: ECC was installed on 2026-09-03T21:24Z. ecc-plugin-assessed-not-mounted.md kept saying 'installed nowhere' until 2026-09-17T20:34Z, through GateGuard fact blocks from 09-04, a 09-06 memory about 'the ECC fact-forcing gate', the founder's 09-13 toolbox paste and the agent's own 09-14 statement that ECC's hooks fired (614500d8).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Treat 'use X whenever necessary' as a standing direction. Write it where the next session starts, and check at session start that X is reachable and used, reading the session's own tool and agent lists rather than assuming.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The same direction came on 09-03, 09-05 and 09-17. It reached says.log (line 768) but no handoff or memory entry. ecc:* agents were listed in adcc31ca from 21:28:15Z, yet 0al said they needed a fresh session. Zero ecc:* calls were made in 59d07e04 and 614500d8. The first use came only after the third statement (70515f55, 2026-09-17T20:40Z).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Judge an outside toolkit by what its content would have caught among the owner's known misses, not only by runtime risk and name matching. Split runtime from content at the first read.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The 09-02 read counted capability matches (0/5/14) and advised against mounting the whole bundle. It took until 09-18, and a founder request, to find rate limiting stated in ECC's security-review, and to reach the 'content kept, hooks off' split that v3.2 already implied.

interaction_lessons.lesson: A delegated decision includes carrying it out. If the change needs explicit permission, such as the owner's global config, ask once for a yes on the exact diff. Do not hand over manual steps and keep listing them as the owner's to-do.
interaction_lessons.evidence: docs/2026-09-19-direction-decisions.md §2: 'handed over, not made', a day after promising to 'act on whatever is reversible'. The agent listed it as the founder's at least five times from 09-19 to 09-22, until the founder said 'let's put the ECC setting edit into settings.json' (2026-09-22T05:50Z). Hours later step 2 went back to him (11053b61 23:44Z, 0bq, 0br, then the 09-23 roadmap).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Do not return a how-question to the owner once they have said such questions belong to the agent. Decide it, write down why, and let them overturn it. Who owns the file bears on who executes the change, not on who decides it.
interaction_lessons.evidence: At 2026-09-18T22:04Z the agent wrote 'Your decision: setting ECC_HOOKS_ENABLED=false', reasoning in 0bm that it was the founder's file and his install. The founder answered 'we'll go with what's best....i know it sounds dumb but I mean it'. design-questions-are-felix-not-founder.md had recorded the same rule on 2026-09-12.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Before recording a decision to switch something off, list what depends on it.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The 09-19 list switched off session:start and stop:cost-tracker. They turned out to be the only resume markers and cost record, found two days later by a usage audit (where-felix-stands §5 item 7).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Measure how another tool's guard behaves before complying with it or building routines around it. Then remove the cost from what the owner reads, and check claims about when a config change takes effect.
interaction_lessons.evidence: 16 'Facts for the gate' blocks appeared in founder-visible prose in 59d07e04 from 09-04. Only on 2026-09-18 did a source read show GateGuard 'reads nothing' and passes a bare retry (ecc-against-v32 §4). On 09-22 the agent twice claimed the settings change applied only to new sessions, and capture stopped within seconds of the edit.

went_well: The 09-02 assessment read ECC at a pinned sha with Felix's own risk functions. It gave a clear answer and put the high-risk install decision with the founder, as invariant 4 requires. Its runtime predictions of a second voice and first-touch friction were later borne out (0bf, direction-decisions §2).

It was honest about method. Handoff 0al states the 09-03 'ECC review' ran as lenses, not ecc:* agents, 'so the word "ECC" above is not taken for more than it was'. That review still produced 7 merged fixes (#144).
The 09-18 read at source cited path:line, marked each claim checked or reported, and separated MODEL_CLAIM mechanisms from tree-bound ones. It found the canonical omission in ECC's own text.

The 09-19 decision used a proposal and a steelman. The steelman kept four guards Felix lacks, instead of an all-off switch, and the delivery mechanism was measured (a settings env entry reaches ECC's hook process).

Step 1 was carried out carefully: backup, JSON validation, a read of ECC's parser, two ids held until the recorder merged and deployed, and the deployed hook driven with a resume payload before the last ids went in.
ECC's reviewer agents were used on engine changes four times (09-17, 09-21) and were credited with real defects (0bi: they 'earned their cost').
capture_gaps: Who ran the install, and why the founder wanted ECC against the recommendation. The install happened outside any transcript; the only stated reason is 'just to understand what is already built' (adcc31ca 2026-09-03T21:28Z).

Whether the two ideas approved on 09-02 (a skill-at-pinned-sha row, AgentShield as a raise-only reader) were deliberately dropped or simply lost. No record addresses them after 09-02 except ecc-against-v32 §3 calling AgentShield 'feasible'.
The founder's reaction to docs/2026-09-18-ecc-against-v32.md itself. His next turn delegated the hooks decision and moved to the thesis.

The total count of GateGuard refusals from 09-03 to 09-22. Felix's ledger could not see JSON denies, so only spot figures exist (1 in 3 parallel first touches, a dozen in one session, about 6% of the rise in Bash calls).
Whether a Workflow script's agents could have taken ecc:* agent types in adcc31ca. The main session had them listed from 21:28:15Z, so 0al's reason fails at least there.
Who will set hooks_enabled false for step 2, and whether the founder wants the roughly 64 MB of captured data deleted.

- 09-05 is counted as sharpening, not repeat, because it widened the 09-03 instruction into a standing way of working.

The episode shows two patterns:
- Founder decisions that change state (install, delegation, approval) reach the record late or not at all.
- The agent treats 'the founder decides' and 'the founder does' as the same thing. 0bm puts it in writing: 'the founder's file... not Felix's to set'.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When you design a consent boundary that re-arms whenever routine artifacts change, put the recurrence cost to the owner as an explicit trade-off: how strict consent should be, and how often it may interrupt. Measure the interruptions and offer a recommended default before shipping. Hash only what the rationale names.
interaction_lessons.evidence: #203 reused the receipt's whole-set hash (eleven tables, now twelve), though its rationale and [!] text name only commissioning.tsv. #218, #241, #261 and #298 staled it. The founder refreshed the receipt by hand at least seven times and re-stamped the grant twice. 0bt: 'blocks every merge until done'. felix merge counts no commission interruptions (53024762 09:02Z). The founder was told the binding on 09-06, never its cost.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When the owner has given a decision in chat, carry it out. Ask again only if something new has come up since.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Keep the owner's part to the irreducible consent act. Running, committing, merging, deploying and notifying around it are the agent's, and any command handed over must be checked to work.

interaction_lessons.lesson: If your own boundary blocks you, satisfy it or escalate the design. Do not quietly route around it.
interaction_lessons.evidence: #243, #245, #247 and #250 were merged through gh while felix merge refused on the stale commission (0bd to 0bg). The agent had said code PRs would wait (614500d8 01:20Z).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Give the owner one stable, named procedure for their act, and keep the terms apart (receipt, grant, run).

intent.final: Unattended work should carry itself. The founder grants a night once, and each session keeps going on its own bounds without clashing with the other sessions running at the same time. Real founder decisions queue for the morning. Direction and state survive a session boundary through a mechanism, not through retyped instructions or a handoff the next session trusts blindly. Session lifetime and context size should be managed without the founder watching them.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When the person who owns the what starts every long run by typing the same operating rules, build them into the system the second time you see them. Don't wait for them to ask for a mode.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The overnight rules were typed on 08-30, 08-31, 09-03, 09-04, 09-05 and 09-12 before the founder asked for a mode "where I don't have to repeat these boring directions" (c79569a0 10:07Z). interaction_lessons.lesson: 'Don't stop unless you must' covers large next items and session boundaries too. Keep going until there is a real blocker, and bank state as you go instead of ending the run to avoid a half-finished item.

On 09-16 he had to ask 'why are we stopping' (614500d8 22:59Z). The 09-05 night showed the right pattern: the handoff updated per piece, about 8.7 hours of work.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Before listing anything as the owner's to do, read who actually holds that authority, and whether it is a mechanics question you can settle yourself. Never create an approval step to feel safe.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The agent said: 'I invented "red tier means the founder merges."' (c79569a0 23:42Z). The night's queue held six merges among nine decisions (0az). The graphify row escalated at the 09-05 close was solved by the founder the next day (59d07e04 09-06T13:19Z). Due maintenance was handed to him twice (09-12T09:55Z, 09-13T18:43Z).

interaction_lessons.lesson: The moment the owner settles a direction, write it where the next session starts, not only in a dated close-out section.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The merge direction was settled 09-12T23:42Z. The next session still queued four merges, and the founder had to say "i thought i made it clear over and over again" (614500d8 23:40Z). Memory records that the direction 'was never written down where a session starts'.

interaction_lessons.lesson: A mechanism built for the owner must be tried under the owner's real conditions soon after it ships, including conditions they have already described, such as many concurrent sessions. Don't leave its first real test to chance.
interaction_lessons.evidence: #222 was used for one night, with its hooks inert (overnight/log.tsv; 0ay). It was keyed per project a month after the 08-14 concurrency direction. Its defects surfaced only when the founder asked to use it again on 09-23 (#307: 36 of 81 assertions fail against main).

interaction_lessons.lesson: A handoff must separate direction from state. Direction is decided; state is a claim the next session re-checks by command.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The 08-10 rewrite labelled everything 'Standing direction — decided, do not ask again' (fa389b5e 22:17Z). The 0bh audit found 11 of 250 claims false and 26 stale. In 0bm a stale blocker was copied forward. #270 had to relabel the session handoff 'not direction'.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When the data contradicts what the owner believes, show them the data, and then still meet the need underneath the belief with something that runs without them. If your own analysis names such a mechanism, decide it rather than ask and let it drop.
interaction_lessons.evidence: The 09-21 measurement found no quality case. The agent recommended the auto-compact window as 'worth trying first', asked instead of setting it, and demoted it to 'Later' the same day (85410a9f 09:32Z; where-felix-stands §6). His dissatisfaction is inferred from his questions; he did not state it.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Test the whole loop the owner cares about (does a night actually keep going), not only the branches you specified. Tests written blind from your own spec share its blind spots.
interaction_lessons.evidence: #222's 47 blind, mutation-tested assertions passed, yet the hook exited at stop_hook_active, which capped every night at one continuation. The agent itself called that exit 'It cannot loop' (0ay versus #307 defect 2). #307's first version again carried an unbounded path (a self re-grant) that only the adversarial review caught.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When the person who owns the what says a class of work should not reach them, make it stick in the same turn. Write the rule where every future session starts, and in the same change remove every sentence in your own tools, PR bodies and notes that says the opposite. Acting correctly in one session is not a fix.

Roadmap v1 made direction-level choices without asking. It reassigned the founder's role ('Fewer design questions, more outreach', v1 §1). It set demand signals that could stop mechanism work ('Fewer than 5 installs by Dec 4 ... stop mechanism work', v1 §5). interaction_lessons.lesson: When the person who owns the what asks 'what would the roadmap look like?', show the draft and wait. A document that records a decision they stated can be merged. A document that makes new what-level decisions (ordering the what, changing their role, setting kill criteria) is direction, and standing authority to merge your own PRs should not cover it until they have read it.
interaction_lessons.evidence: #290 transcribed an explicit decision and was never objected to. #293 made new decisions, was merged 03:10:04Z with the PDF ready since 02:51Z, and was rejected 03:13:53Z; #295 needed 34 minutes and a second gate to undo it (46af4fa6).

interaction_lessons.lesson: Never change the owner's role inside a plan. If a plan needs a new kind of work from them, such as outreach, recruiting or threshold-setting, ask it as an explicit outcome question: 'do you want your next months to go to finding users or to building?'
interaction_lessons.evidence: Roadmap v1 §1 'The founder's part. Fewer design questions, more outreach' and §6 windows; chat 03:10Z '你的角色变了。设计问题少了，找用户多了'; rejected 03:13Z.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Carry the owner's qualifiers into the plan, especially when they rest on your own facts. When your critics split and one dissent matches the owner's qualifier, show the split instead of synthesising it away. 'Only a scaffold, don't worry about paying yet' outranks a critic majority or an imported brief's validation plan.

went_well: The agent grounded the founder's imported brief against code, doctrine and first-hand market sources, and had critics attack its own theses before answering. It told him which of its theses had fallen (00:52Z).
It named the identity question as his alone and cited the standing records that said no (charter, August brief), instead of deciding it or burying it (00:52Z).

It turned the decision into doctrine within 51 minutes (#290). It changed only the scope paragraphs, stated what stays (engineering-only), re-gated after a red run caused by a moved main, and disclosed that red run.

It answered the Factory question with verified facts: droid exec is self-serve, the REST API is org-gated, and the terms bar competing products. It reframed the Capability Plane around qualifying judges, and the founder accepted that (02:02Z to 02:17Z).

It ran the discovery request through a Plan subagent on a clean clone to avoid priming, and downgraded its own result to calibration when the hole turned out to be known (03:10Z; lessons.md 2026-09-22).
It corrected its own claims in the open: Droid hours, the arming default, and the Elenchus hit.

After the rejection it did not argue. The rewrite kept the harvest and critic work (mechanism order, §7 corrections), added 'build the class' (Elenchus plus one other ecosystem), and landed with handoff and memory in 34 minutes. The founder later called it 'updated quite well' (654dc33f 08:53Z), and a later session executed its Phase 0 (207f7bdf).
The founder spent very little effort: five short prompts across the arc (~880 characters).
capture_gaps: The 6-page continuation brief and both roadmap PDFs exist only in the session scratchpad and on the founder's device (HANDOFF 0bs: 'their Markdown was scratch'). The critic verdicts behind his 01:09Z decision are not in the repo; they survive only in the session's task output files.
The ChatGPT conversation behind the brief is not in the corpus; only its PDF summary is.
Whether the founder read the 6-page PDF (sent 00:52Z) before deciding at 01:09Z, and whether he read the roadmap v1 PDF or only the chat summary before rejecting at 03:13Z, is unknown.

The interaction failure is visible only in the transcript.

notes:
Counting: the five founder turns are labelled by their primary kind, which gives 0 leakage turns. Two turns carry smaller leakage components.
- 01:09Z restated the settled two-plane endgame after the agent's 'Capability Plane stays thin' (a leakage-repeat-settled component).
- 02:17Z's 'ok' approved a mechanics default that the amendments had already settled (a leakage-answered-agent-question component). The agent was prompted to ask by a stale qualify.sh header.

The 03:13Z turn is labelled direction-feedback. It carries a caught-overreach component, because he had asked about the months of building and got back a merged plan that reassigned him to outreach. His words object to content (build first vs demand first), not to the merge. The turn also sharpens his own 01:09Z 'commercialisation as direction' wording, which on its face supported a demand-first reading. It ends with an operational 'handoff' that accepts the agent's 03:10Z offer.

The 2026-09-14 turn is counted because the task names it as the earlier distribution question. The personal second prompt in that session was skipped. Felix had been public since 2026-09-13, so that turn is a channel question, not the origin of the product idea.

Where the outreach framing came from:
- The founder's own imported ChatGPT brief proposed 8-12 weeks of external validation and called demand the largest gap (discussion.txt §1, §8.4).
- The agent's own thesis T9 said the same. Two positioning critics upheld T9. One weakened it because the differentiating mechanism had zero instances.
- Both roadmap critics recommended a demand-led synthesis ('Lead with demand'; 'Use the user-first draft's calendar').
- The agent put 'find 5-10 external users' in its first proposal at 00:52Z, and the founder did not reject it at 01:09Z.

So the agent did not invent the outreach framing. Its error was promoting it to the lead track, reassigning his role and merging that as doctrine before he read it.

On the E01 comparison: E01's split (felix-is-the-implementation-pilot.md) lists 'pitching' under the founder. The conflict is that v1 made him the operator of a demand experiment that gates engineering, and assigned him threshold pre-registration, which is design work.

Timeline check: #293 merged 03:10:04Z and the founder rejected it 03:13:53Z (3m49s later), 20:10 and 20:13 PDT on 2026-09-22. It was the same day in either zone.

Founder input totalled about 880 characters across the five prompts (prompts.tsv lengths 86+166+442+60+124). Agent-side spend was about 3.5M subagent tokens.

interaction_lessons.lesson: The person who owns the 'what' should never have to know that a sentence is machine-read. Before rewording any output text, the agent should search for everything that reads it. Where a reader exists, it should pin the pairing with a test that renders the real producer's text, not a fixture's copy.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Scope a review by what could break, not by the author's own account of the change. When a change edits text, a format or an exit code, the brief should state that edit and add a lens asking who consumes it.

interaction_lessons.lesson: Know which copy the running system executes. A change to a file the home checkout reads takes effect when the home pulls, not when a PR merges or an engine deploys. Live verification has to watch that moment.

notes:
Architecture-level reading. Felix's mistake accounting (mistakes.log, which feeds felix promote and rank 5 of felix next) depends on a contract carried in prose across the engine/project boundary. A project-owned gate.sh prints a human sentence, and the engine greps one word out of it. Only Felix's own gate emits the marker; no other projects/*/gate.sh contains 'structural'. The engine documented the contract at the consumer (engine/harness/felix:700-716) and not at the producer until #123. The same word carried opposite meanings for its two readers, and that is the root of the episode. The agent removed 'structural' because it had misled a human reader, the agent itself at 23:15Z, and in doing so broke the machine reader.

A second structural fact surfaced in this check. felix gate executes the home checkout's working copy of gate.sh, not the gate.sh of the tree under test (~/.felix-home; felix_home in resolve.sh; stated in 0ebfa7d0). A gate change therefore takes effect in every worktree the moment the home pulls, independent of merge or deploy, and the tree's own copy is not what judges it. That is why the regression went live on the agent's 03:50Z pull and not at the 00:35Z merge, and why the 09:30Z probe still recorded a row. This is an early instance of the class 'a contract between files carried in an untyped string'. Linking it to the later rows-first/typed-record direction (memory bash-as-architecture-critique, #298 schemas.tsv) is this reader's inference and is not recorded anywhere.

On the pipeline, the whole episode ran with zero founder leakage. Issue, fix, regression, detection and correction were all on the agent's side, and Felix's own mechanisms (the Stop hook and felix next) triggered both corrections. The detection path was lucky. The regression surfaced only because its symptom was the top line of felix next. The agent first missed it in its own gate output (03:52Z) and then dismissed it (07:49Z). The misleading top row outlived the fix and drove #179 five days later.

Minor: the #115 PR body still says 984 assertions, while the merged head, after the review repairs, records 991.

The two 09:17Z prompts are counted as two founder turns; the first was a typo that the second corrected. The founder's 21:59Z and 22:02Z turns (a network change, then 'continue') fall in the 21:32Z to 23:15Z window but concern nothing in this episode, so they are not counted.

Confidence is high for the timeline and mechanism. They were read from the transcripts (including tool output at 03:47Z, 03:52Z and 09:30Z), the PR diffs, the commit messages and the code. The row attribution rests on a log that records only dates, so it is medium outside rows 27 and 28.

The first working copy of the fix ran the judge-identity check through the candidate CLI's own resolve.sh, which recreates self-judgement. The understand map and critic caught it before the PR (70515f55 ~02:56Z).

The design doc says #260 was 'closed the same day'. It was filed 2026-09-17T23:54Z and closed 2026-09-18T21:35Z; only the PR opened on the same Pacific day (docs/2026-09-17-exception-channel-design.md:94-96).

Letting the handoff and the distance table say 'judge pinned for felix merge' while the override defeated it.
Summarising the audit to the founder as having found no false claims about code behaviour when it had.

Copying the 'still waits on you' status forward without reading commissioning.log.

interaction_lessons.lesson: When you deliver the owner's chosen option with a known limit that undercuts the reason they chose it, file the limit as an open defect and tell the owner plainly that their choice is not fully delivered yet. A limit framed as a deliberate choice decays: its justification can lapse unnoticed, and later records start claiming the property holds.

went_well: The agent closed a filed authority hole on its own initiative. It needed no founder design input, and the founder spent no leakage turns.

The design question (flag versus identity check) was settled inside Felix. The rejected alternative and the reason are in the PR body ('Why not a flag'), in line with design-questions-are-felix-not-founder.md.
It reused the gate's existing question (felix_accepted_deploy_diff through main's own resolve.sh, from #256) instead of re-deriving it, following the promotion spec's 'Call it. Do not re-derive it.'

It used blind assertions and a critic together. 10 of the 14 blind assertions are shown red on file against 0.49.121. The critic caught two defects the blind author could not see: the && exit status and the self-sourced identity check.
It repaired the fixture's premise instead of weakening the new rule, and recorded that as a lesson.
The residuals it did see (tables from the home FELIX_HOME chooses, no verifier confine on the CLI and libraries) are named in §0bk and §0bl rather than implied away.
The success path names the judge on stdout and in says.log. The fix was visibly verified at first real use (21:45Z), and says.log now makes it possible to count which merges went through the pin.
Felix merged its own red-tier PR once the founder's reserved step was done, per standing direction, and gated the squash commit once the Stop hook flagged it.
The session-close audit caught the handoff's false 'judge pinned' claim and recorded the correction in §0bl before the next session relied on it.
capture_gaps: There is no founder reaction to #260 or #263 anywhere in the prompt index, so the outcome verdict rests on the later record, not on his judgement.
The founder was told about the override three times in August, but nothing shows whether he registered it, or why no issue was filed then.
The founder's commission re-stamp is known only from commissioning.log and §0bm's reasoning by elimination. Whether the handoff's request prompted it is unrecorded.

Partly answered: in 10793b58 both merges ran from the deployed cache CLI. Across other sessions, which CLI runs felix merge is unmeasured, and §0bl notes a branch that deletes the refusal sets no escape.
Unmeasured: whether a session can make origin/main absent, which is what the local-main fallback in felix_kernel_dir and felix_base_ref needs.
How 8 of the 10 merges without a felix merge record were made (#274, #276-#279, #292, #294, #296) was not checked. Only #297 (plain gh by a session) and #285 (gh after founder approval) were.
No issue or handoff entry schedules the 2026-09-20 residue-rule fix or the 2026-09-21 superseded-CLI refusal. The latter is listed as the founder's decision.

'git log -S FELIX_KERNEL 53eaf249..origin/main' returns #268, #269, #276, #283 and #285. #269 (docs/2026-09-21-where-felix-stands.md) is a substantive later correction: the hole persists via superseded cached CLIs. For the founder's 'fundamental and architectural' lens: this is the trust-root decision of the authority kernel (amendments §2.3). The founder chose a free, locally pinned judge over GitHub Pro. The delivery pinned judge identity at felix merge, but by 2026-09-21 the record classes that as a floor and hands the wall back to him. That is the architectural outcome to read, more than #263's engineering, which was careful.
